title: Exact constant realization with regular and quotient units
statement: Let C be a small category, J a Grothendieck topology, A a commutative Noetherian ring and I an ideal. For either constant or completed coefficient sheaf O_b [def-sfb-constant-completion-coefficient-data], there is an additive functor E:ModuleCat A -> Mod O_b preserving finite limits and finite colimits, an isomorphism c:unit O_b -> E(A), and isomorphisms q_n:E(A/I^(n+1)) -> restriction along finiteMap_b,n of the regular finite quotient sheaf. For each x in A, c followed by E(multiplication by x) is multiplication by algebraSection(baseMap_b)(x) followed by c. For each n, c followed by E(the quotient map) and q_n is the unit-module map given by the compatible section 1 of the restricted finite quotient. This contains no complexes, Koszul comparison, cones or inverse limits.

source.place: Tags 093M and 03EK; Tag 099M, scalar realization of the finite quotients.

proof.text: Construct E as commutativeSiteConstantModuleFunctor J A followed by ordinary change of rings along baseMap. Constant module realization is exact. Change of rings is exact because its restricted target unit is flat: for b=true use flat_and_quotients, and for b=false use the identity coefficient map and the tensor unitor. Thus E is additive and preserves finite limits and colimits.

Define generator(m) by the scalar-extension adjunction unit applied to the constant module sheafification unit at m. The compatible sections generator(1) give oneMap:unit -> E(A). The tensor adjunction, sheafification Hom equivalence, and the regular-presheaf sections equivalence show that precomposition with oneMap is bijective on every Hom set. Hence oneMap is invertible by the coyoneda criterion. Naturality and linearity of the two adjunction units give the multiplication formula.

Transpose the actual constant quotient map through the two adjunctions to define quotientMap:E(A/I^(n+1)) -> restricted finite unit. It sends generator(class(a)) to the corresponding constant quotient section. The map b -> b*generator(1) kills the kernel of the sectionwise finite projection: flat_and_quotients describes this kernel as the span of the images of I^(n+1). Descend this map through the surjective finite projection on every site object; lifting sections proves compatibility with restrictions. The two inverse identities are checked on constant generators and on lifted quotient sections. Thus quotientMap is invertible.

For the quotient normalization, use the unit-module sections equivalence and evaluate at 1 on every site object. Naturality sends generator(1) to generator(class(1)); quotientMap sends it to the finite section 1. These constructions also work for I=0, I=A, zero rings and empty sites.

lean.statement:
theorem constantExactCoefficientRealization
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (b : Bool) :
    ∃ (E : ModuleCat.{u} A ⥤ Mod (coefficients J A I b)) (_hadd : E.Additive)
      (_hlim : PreservesFiniteLimits E) (_hcolim : PreservesFiniteColimits E)
      (c : SheafOfModules.unit (siteModuleRings (coefficients J A I b)) ≅
        E.obj (ModuleCat.of A A))
      (q : ∀ n : ℕ, E.obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))) ≅
        (res (finiteMap J A I b n)).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (siteModuleRings (finite J A I n)))),
      (∀ x : A, c.hom ≫ E.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.mul A A x)) =
        ringedKoszulScalar (coefficients J A I b) (algebraSection (baseMap J A I b) x) ≫
          c.hom) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, c.hom ≫ E.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (I ^ (n + 1)).mkQ) ≫ (q n).hom =
        (SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv
          ((res (finiteMap J A I b n)).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit (siteModuleRings (finite J A I n))))).symm
          ⟨fun V ↦ (1 : (finite J A I n).obj.obj V),
            fun f ↦ map_one ((finite J A I n).obj.map f).hom⟩
